summary: Storefront editor upgrade stage 1 (owner D4 Option 1): real page in the editor + scroll-effect presets — spec, critique, build in 3 streams, adversarial review, fix

result.risks:
1. Server Action returning RSC is the core bet. Next 14.2 supports returning React elements from actions, but this repo has never used a Server Action, and next/dynamic client sections plus server-component CSS (brand.css, servd.css, stackd.css, crossBrand.css) must reach the frame. Importing the action from app/editor-frame/page.tsx should keep them in the route graph. If the screenshots show missing brand CSS, import those group CSS files directly in page.tsx. Plan B if action-returned RSC fails outright: an in-memory per-token doc store written by a server action, with router.refresh() on /editor-frame?t=<token> (single storefront process).
2. Next's Server Action CSRF check compares Origin with Host / x-forwarded-host. If the Cloudflare tunnel rewrites Host, every render fails with "Invalid Server Actions request". The contract adds experimental.serverActions.allowedOrigins = [SERVD host]. Verify on prod.
3. Any edge layer (Cloudflare Transform Rule, tunnel) that adds X-Frame-Options globally would block the frame. Check with curl -sI https://servd.pk/editor-frame after deploy. ADMIN_ORIGINS is unset in prod today, so the default https://admin.servd.pk applies. Any other admin host (staging, local sims on :3200) must set it. The storefront-sections CORS default stops allowing localhost in production as a side effect (harmless).
4. Scroll-driven CSS ships in Chrome/Edge 115+ and Safari 26+. Firefox may still be flag-only. Everyone else uses the JS engine, which needs CSSAnimation.currentTime and getAnimations() (Safari 13.1+, Firefox 75+). In the fallback, an element already on screen at load can visibly jump to its scroll state once JS starts. Named-range math in JS must match CSS: view-timeline-inset is pinned to 0 for that reason.
5. Effects on whole blocks have built-in trade-offs:
   - Parallax and side-pan can show page background at the edges of full-bleed coloured bands.
   - Pin and stack hide part of a block taller than the screen.
   - A lone sticky-stack block does nothing.
   - Stack cards rely on --sv-page-bg, computed from the brand surface only on brand pages rendered with a section context.
   - Transforms change the containing block for fixed/absolute descendants inside an animated block.
   - Sections that already move on scroll (servd scroll-expansion hero, Simmer fridge hero, Stackd stickers) can fight an added preset.
   - The servd home hero holds the page still while it expands, in the frame as on live.
   - --sv-sticky-top (52 px under the servd nav) uses :has(). On brand pages, pins sit at top 0, under any fixed or sticky brand header.
6. Every edit re-renders the whole page on the storefront server, which also calls the API for concepts, chrome layouts and section data. This is bounded by the 250 ms admin throttle, single-flight latest-wins in the frame, a 600/min per-IP action limit and 30 s caches for chrome and concepts. Internal API calls are exempt from the API rate limiter, but heavy editing adds load to the same container that serves customers. Action payloads run up to about 200–600 KB per render on slow links.
7. The Server Action is a public endpoint. Anyone can ask the storefront to render arbitrary block JSON plus public data. No secrets are exposed and the output is not HTML, but it costs CPU and API calls; the in-memory rate limit is only per process and per IP.
8. Fidelity gaps by design:
   - Surrounding chrome is always shown as variant A.
   - Brand pages render on servd.pk (onBrandHost false), so brand-domain-only link forms differ.
   - servd:location previews the first location.
   - The frame's chrome sits inside <main>.
   - Trackers, JSON-LD and the search sheet are absent.
   - Next <Link> prefetches inside the frame hit other routes, which may set the sv_vid visitor cookie in the operator's browser.
   - An emptied built-in page shows its default design unmarked (true to live).
   - Section internals are not selectable.
9. Desktop preview at ~0.4–0.5 scale on a 1440 px screen with the AppShell sidebar open is small. Operators can switch device or collapse the sidebar. A zoom control is a later stage.
10. Pre-existing security issue: core block links (hero, banner, CTA) and media URLs are not run through safe.ts, so a javascript: href in an approved hero would execute on the live site. The frame blocks activation (all clicks and keys are captured). The contract includes a SHOULD that neutralises script schemes only.
11. Untouched pages cannot be opened while the storefront (catalogue) is unreachable, because their design comes from it. Pages with a saved draft or live blocks open, but section forms are read-only in effect.
12. The editor frame and the live renderer share code. A bug in BlockSlot wrapping would affect every live page. Mitigation: byte-identical HTML regression check on pages without motion (test plan step 3).
13. Docs drift to fix at integration: CLAUDE.md still names components/brand/layouts/* (now sections) and says framer-motion and three are dependencies (they are not). The task brief's "tree.ts undo" does not exist.

amendments.area: security / storefront renderer (SSRF through the public server action)
amendments.problem: components/blocks/FeaturedMenu.tsx:16 and Reviews.tsx:17 put block.conceptSlug into the internal API URL without encoding: fetch(`${API_URL}/api/v1/storefront/${slug}/menu`). Today only approved layouts reach this. With /editor-frame, anyone on the internet can call renderEditorFrame with a block such as {type:'featured_menu', conceptSlug:'../../anything?x='}. The storefront server then makes unauthenticated GETs to arbitrary internal-API paths. Those calls skip the API rate limiter (risk 6), and because the fetches use next.revalidate, every distinct URL also adds an entry to Next's on-disk fetch cache. sanitize.ts in the contract validates only id/type and leaves all other fields unchecked.
amendments.change: (a) Add FeaturedMenu.tsx and Reviews.tsx to S's file list. Wrap the slug in encodeURIComponent(slug). For valid slugs the output is byte-identical. (b) sanitize.ts: on featured_menu/reviews/kitchens blocks, drop `conceptSlug` unless it matches /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,59}$/. Apply the same check to any section field the action resolves into a fetch. (c) README note in src/editor: every value a renderer puts into a server-side URL must be encoded, because the action renders unauthenticated input.

amendments.problem: The only bound on the public server action is 600 renders per minute per IP. Each render is a full page composition plus several internal API calls (section data is fetched on every render, and internal calls are rate-limit exempt). With rotating IPs or a spoofed x-forwarded-for, this amplifies load against the API and starves the customer storefront in the same container. A real editor session is single-flight, so it never needs more than one render in flight per frame.
amendments.change: limits.ts: (1) Use a global in-process concurrency cap of 4 renders in flight. When the cap is reached, return RATE_LIMITED immediately without queueing. (2) Lower the per-IP limit to 240/min. Key on cf-connecting-ip only when the request came through the tunnel; otherwise use the first x-forwarded-for hop, as the contract says. (3) Bound the in-memory IP map: prune entries older than 60 s and cap it at 10k keys. (4) Never log the input. On error, log only code, slug and size. Add a test-plan item: 10 parallel action calls → at most 4 render and the rest get RATE_LIMITED.

amendments.problem: The negative lookahead `/:path((?!editor-frame).*)` also strips X-Frame-Options from /editor-frame-anything and /editor-frame/anything. The middleware sets the CSP only for `/editor-frame` and `/editor-frame/`, so those other paths (404 pages) can be framed by any site. The frame route also answers on brand hosts (stackd.pk/editor-frame), which is extra surface for no use.
amendments.change: next.config.js: use `source: '/:path((?!editor-frame(?:/|$)).*)'`. Middleware: on the editor-frame path, when the host is not a servd host (isServdHost(bare) false, localhost allowed in dev), rewrite to a 404 instead of passing through. Only the servd host serves the frame.

amendments.problem: §6.2 sends `error PROTOCOL` to `ev.origin` for a foreign-version message without checking ev.source. The frame also renders pop-up docs entirely client-side (§4.4.3) from posted JSON that never goes through sanitize.ts.
amendments.change: Reply with PROTOCOL only when ev.source === window.parent AND ev.origin is allowed. Make sanitize.ts isomorphic (no 'server-only', no next/headers). Run the same block/settings/fonts sanitiser in EditorFrameClient on pop-up docs before building the LivePopup. Also enforce settings.popup.display ∈ {modal,bar,corner}, else 'modal'.

amendments.problem: The SHOULD that neutralises script hrefs in Hero/Banner/CtaButton is the only guard on live pages. The frame's click/key capture does not cover link drags: dragging an <a href='javascript:…'> out of the frame onto admin inputs works. React 18 only warns on javascript: URLs.
amendments.change: Promote the Hero/Banner/CtaButton script-scheme neutralisation from SHOULD to MUST, with the exact rule already in the contract. Also capture `dragstart` on window in the frame and preventDefault it. Stage-7 drag will define its own drag handling.

amendments.problem: When a doc is rejected for TOO_LARGE or BAD_DOC, the frame posts `error` with no rev. The admin has postedRev > renderedRev forever, so it stays on 'Updating…' and the preview slider stays disabled. Errors thrown by the action call itself are also unhandled: network failure, 413 over bodySizeLimit, 'Failed to find Server Action' after a storefront redeploy (version skew), and the Next CSRF 'Invalid Server Actions request'. The contract only handles errors returned as a result.
amendments.change: (1) protocol.ts: add `rev: number | null` to the `error` message. Alternatively, and preferred: say that any failure for a doc is answered with `rendered{rev, ok:false, error}`, and `error` is kept for session-level problems only. (2) EditorFrameClient: wrap `await render(...)` in try/catch → rendered{ok:false, error:'The live page could not be updated.'}. If the thrown message matches /Server Action/i (stale deploy), call location.reload() once per session (guard with sessionStorage). The admin already re-sends init on the new `ready`.

amendments.problem: MAX_DOC_CHARS and the 600_000 check count UTF-16 code units, but bodySizeLimit '1mb' counts bytes of the encodeReply body. A doc of 600k chars of Urdu or emoji is about 1.8 MB, so the action is rejected opaquely with 413 even though both checks passed.
amendments.change: Measure UTF-8 bytes (new TextEncoder().encode(json).length) in both the frame and sanitize.ts, with a cap of 600_000 bytes. Set serverActions.bodySizeLimit to '2mb'. The stored content is still bounded by the backend's MAX_CONTENT_BYTES of 200_000.

amendments.problem: §4.4.4 puts the error boundary 'keyed by rev'. Changing a key remounts the whole subtree, so every keystroke unmounts and remounts the entire page. That resets client state in every section (the scroll-expansion hero, the Stackd stickers, carousels), restarts videos, re-runs entrance animations (.sv-anim drops back to opacity 0), and can make the scroll position jump. The page would flicker on every edit.
amendments.change: Do not key the boundary by rev. Use one long-lived boundary class that stores {error, errorRev} and clears the error in getDerivedStateFromProps when props.rev !== state.errorRev, i.e. the resetKeys pattern. The reconciled tree must keep the same element types and keys across revs, so the commit is an in-place update.

amendments.problem: A single half-typed or malformed block crashes the whole frame back to lastGood. Hero primaryCta set to a string gives a Next <Link href={undefined}> throw; gallery.images set to a non-array throws in .map. Most core-block fields go unvalidated by both the backend (passthrough) and sanitize.ts. Server-component errors stream to the nearest client boundary.
amendments.change: In editor mode, make the selection marker a small client component (src/editor/BlockMarker.tsx, 'use client', renders <div data-sv-block data-sv-type style={{display:'contents'}}>) holding its own error boundary. The fallback is a thin dashed placeholder, 'This element can't be drawn yet', using storefront tokens. That way one bad block never blanks the page, and `rendered` can report it (add the failed ids to `rendered.error` text, or leave the id among the ids). Live pages are unaffected because markers are frame-only.

amendments.problem: PopupFrame's effect runs `cardRef.current?.focus()` and depends on [display, onClose]. If the frame passes an inline no-op onClose, the effect re-runs on every render and calls focus() inside the iframe every time the operator types in the inspector. Where the browser allows it, keyboard focus is pulled out of the admin input mid-keystroke.
amendments.change: PopupFrame gets `editor?: boolean`. When it is set, skip the focus() call, and the frame passes a module-level constant NOOP for onClose so the effect never re-runs. Keep the body overflow lock, because that matches live.

amendments.problem: §6.3 says the admin does not echo `select` back, but says nothing about hover. If the admin re-posts hover after a frame hover, the two sides ping-pong.
amendments.change: Track the source for hover exactly as for select. A frame-originated hover updates the Layers highlight only and is never posted back. Only hover that starts in Layers is posted.

amendments.problem: Desktop height = floor(H/k) gives viewports like 1280×1600. Every 100vh/100dvh hero, vh/vw-based effect range and pin track then renders as no real desktop would, so the preview and the slider mislead on exactly what this stage is about.
amendments.change: Desktop viewport = 1280 × 800, k = min(1, W/1280, H/800). Show the device box centred like phone and tablet. Use the read-out 'Desktop · 1280×800 · 44%'.

amendments.problem: Client sections are next/dynamic (sections/<group>/lazy.ts). In an action-returned tree a newly mounted one shows its null loading fallback first, then fills in. Rects measured 'after commit' are null or stale, and ResizeObserver only watches already-measured elements.
amendments.change: In EditorFrameClient, run a MutationObserver (childList+subtree, rAF-debounced) on #sv-editor-root and the pop-up layer. It redraws outlines, re-applies a pending motion preview, and re-observes measured elements.

amendments.area: motion / presets (content must end fully visible)
amendments.problem: Several ranges end at points that the last blocks on a page can never reach: fade strong `cover 50%`, grow `cover 45%`, text-reveal `cover 50%`, and pin-reveal `exit-crossing 0% + track`. Near the end of a document, and always for footer blocks (footer kind is offered), the element can't scroll that far, so it stays faded, shrunk, faint or inset-clipped forever. Side-pan is continuous over `cover`, so at max scroll the last block stays shifted up to about 0.6 × 26vw and text is cut off by body overflow-x: clip. Tall top-of-page blocks start partly faint or small too. This breaks the contract's own rule that content ends fully visible.
amendments.change: (1) Change ranges so every preset that hides content reaches its natural state by `entry 100%`. `entry 100%` is always reachable: the bottom of the last block meets the viewport bottom at max scroll. Use fade: subtle `entry 0% entry 60%`, medium/strong `entry 0% entry 100%`. Use grow: `entry 0% entry 100%`. Use text-reveal: `entry 0% entry 100%`. Make side-pan slide in: @keyframes sv-m-pan from translate3d(var(--sv-m-x),0,0) to none, range `entry 0% entry 100%`. Parallax stays continuous; its strong value is only a y-offset. (2) Add an end-reachability guard to MotionRuntime that runs in ALL browsers when hasMotion. On load, resize and DOM change, for each keyframed wrapper compute s_max = V − (wrapperDocTop − maxScrollY) and the range end s1 with rangeProgress math. If s_max < s1 − 1, set `data-sv-motion-off` and add CSS `.sv-motion[data-sv-motion-off] > .sv-motion-target, .sv-motion[data-sv-motion-off] > .sv-motion-pin > .sv-motion-target { animation: none !important }`. This mainly protects pin-reveal. (3) Admin: offer pin-reveal and sticky-stack for kind `page` only, not footer. Update the §2.1 table, MOTION_SPECS, the §7.5 slider start/end text and the mobile entrance map wording (side-pan → slide-left is still right).

amendments.area: motion / kinds that must never move
amendments.problem: Motion is gated only in the admin UI (page/footer). The backend accepts motion on any block of any kind, and the renderer applies it wherever it finds it. A motion value saved through the API (or carried in by copy) on servd:feedback or a header wraps the fixed feedback button or the sticky .sv-nav in a transformed or clipped target. That breaks position:fixed/sticky site-wide.
amendments.change: SiteLayoutView: when layout.kind is 'header', 'widget' or 'popup', pass `motion: false` in RenderContext. renderSlots then skips normalizeMotion. Live HTML for those kinds is byte-identical to today.

(a) sections/servd/Feedback.tsx treats only /preview as a preview (isPreviewPath). In the frame the draft feedback button follows the cooldown and route rules, so it can hide itself, and its submit path is live. (b) An empty custom brand page `brand::

amendments.problem: The admin maps a family to 'the first matching Library font'. Live uses resolveFonts (backend service.ts): the layout company's assets, newest upload wins. An operator with several companies can see a different font in the frame than on the live page.
amendments.change: LiveCanvas: for each family, choose among Library fonts with the same tenantId as the edited brand's company (from STOREFRONT_BRANDS_KEY / concept.tenantId; servd:* and page:* use any). Sort by createdAt descending, mirroring resolveFonts. Document this in the storefront README.

amendments.problem: 'pass params: { loc } = the first location from fetchBrandLocations (sorted by name)' is ambiguous. fetchBrandLocations returns a Record keyed by brand slug, while the location sections and findLocation expect `loc` to be a BrandLocation.locationSlug. When nothing matches and the API is down, findLocation throws BrandListUnavailableError.

amendments.problem: The stack card's soft box-shadow is a blurred dark gradient edge, and the stack card gets servd ink in its shadow even on Simmer pages, which ban gradients.
amendments.change: motion.css: `.sv-stack-card:has(.simmer-page) { box-shadow: none; }` (or drop the shadow whenever --sv-page-bg is a brand surface). Add Simmer to the §7.5 Simmer note.

But Motion.tsx imports motion.css from PageRenderer's graph, which the root layout reaches through servd:header, so every page gains new CSS, and MotionRuntime adds a client module. The orchestrator would read that diff as a regression, or wave it through without looking.

amendments.problem: Risk 1 is only checked after screenshots. A clean prevention costs nothing.
amendments.change: In app/editor-frame/page.tsx, import the four group CSS files directly (sections/brand/brand.css, simmer/simmer.css, simmer/crossBrand.css, stackd/stackd.css, servd/servd.css) and `import '../../sections/renderers'` as a side effect. Every section's CSS and client references are then in this route's manifest whether or not Next traverses into the 'use server' module.

built.summary:
Stream S (storefront) is built. It covers the editor frame route, the block markers, the scroll-effect renderer and CSS, the header and CSP policy, the motion types, pop-ups shown in the frame, and the docs. `npx tsc` passes, and a scratch check of the motion maths, sanitiser and limits passes.

**Live page in the editor**
- New route `/editor-frame`: `page.tsx` + `actions.ts`, with `src/editor/{EditorFrameClient.tsx, FrameDocument.tsx, BlockMarker.tsx, protocol.ts, types.ts, sanitize.ts, limits.ts, README.md}`.
- The server action `renderEditorFrame` sanitises the posted draft, rate-limits it, and fetches the live chrome around it. It returns an RSC tree of `FrameDocument`, built with the real renderers (ManagedPage / SiteLayoutView / PageRenderer / BrandShell). The document follows every row of contract §4.3.
- Every part renders with `previewVariant`, so there is no TrackedLayout and no SiteLayoutStat. The frame never fetches a draft and never reads cookies or auth.
- The frame client:
  - **Messaging:** strict origin, source and session locking. It announces `ready` to the referrer origin, or to each allowed origin. It never posts with `'*'`.
  - **Rendering:** single-flight, latest doc wins. Results are committed in place with `startTransition`. A long-lived boundary resets when the rev changes, so the page is not remounted on each edit (UX-1).
  - **Per-block safety:** a per-block BlockMarker error boundary (UX-2).
  - **Outlines:** selection, hover and context outlines are drawn on a fixed overlay. Labels are set as text only. The overlay redraws on scroll, resize, ResizeObserver and a MutationObserver on the root (UX-6).
  - **Input capture:** clicks, middle clicks, submit, Escape (selects the parent), Enter/Space on links and buttons, and dragstart (SEC-5) never reach the page.
  - **Preview slider:** scrubs the effect in place; sticky-stack scrolls the page instead.
  - **Pop-ups:** sanitised on the client (SEC-4) and drawn with the exported `PopupFrame` in editor mode (no focus steal, a constant no-op close; UX-3). A bar pop-up sits in flow above the page; modal and corner are fixed. They show over the targeted brand home, or over servd home.
- **Chrome stands down:** the root layout's nav, footer, feedback slot and PopupHost stand down on this path through `lib/editorFrame.ts`. PopupHost skips its fetch, keeps its hook order, and has `editor-frame` in RESERVED.
- **Headers:** `lib/adminOrigins.ts` is the one definition, also now used by `/api/storefront-sections`.
  - The middleware sends `CSP frame-ancestors <ADMIN_ORIGINS>` on `/editor-frame` only. It sets no visitor cookie, does no settle or rewrite, and drops the brand header.
  - On a non-servd host, or a case variant of the path, it rewrites to a 404 with `frame-ancestors 'none'` and `X-Frame-Options: DENY` (SEC-3).
  - `next.config.js`:
    - X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN is kept on `/`, on `/:path((?!editor-frame(?:/|$)).*)` and on `/editor-frame/:rest+`.
    - `/editor-frame` gets the other base headers plus `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`.
    - Added `experimental.serverActions { allowedOrigins: [SERVD_URL.host], bodySizeLimit: '2mb' }` (PROTO-2).

**Scroll effects**
- `lib/motion.ts` holds MOTION_SPECS (values follow FID-1: fade/grow/text-reveal end at `entry 100%`, side-pan slides in over the same range), plus `normalizeMotion`, `rangeCss`, `motionVars`, `rangeSpan`/`rangeProgress` and `hasMotion`.
- `components/blocks/{Motion.tsx, motion.css, motionClient.ts, MotionRuntime.tsx}`:
  - The CSS uses scroll-driven animations under `@supports`, a fallback that only applies once JS marks the wrapper ready, the editor scrub rule, and a reduced-motion reset.
  - The JS engine is loaded on demand. It includes the FID-1 reach guard (`data-sv-motion-off`), which runs in every browser but not for parallax.
- PageRenderer wraps each block in this order: editor marker → MotionWrap → BlockSlot. It groups runs of sticky-stack blocks into `.sv-stack`.
  - With no motion and outside the editor, it takes a fast path that returns exactly today's elements.
  - In the editor, a block whose data fetch fails becomes a thrown element, so only that block's boundary shows a placeholder.
- SiteLayoutView passes `motion:false` for header, widget and pop-up layouts (FID-2) and mounts MotionRuntime only when the blocks have motion.
- ManagedPage gets `editor` and `editorMarker` props, used on the given/live-layout branch only.
- `lib/blocks.ts` gets the motion types, `motion?: BlockMotion`, `blockHref()` (SEC-5), and a fixed header comment.

**Other changes**
- `sections/pageSurface.tsx` is now used by home, press, reserve and locations with the same markup (confirm with step 3).
- `encodeURIComponent` in FeaturedMenu and Reviews; the sanitiser also drops invalid `conceptSlug` (SEC-1).
- Feedback treats the frame as a preview (FID-3a). Empty custom pages get the editor-only note (FID-3b).
- servd:location uses the first publishable location by name, or a "No location to preview yet." notice (FID-5).
- No stack shadow on brand pages (FID-6).
- `limits.ts`: 4 renders in flight server-wide, otherwise RATE_LIMITED at once; 240 per minute per IP, using cf-connecting-ip only when cf-ray is present, else the first X-Forwarded-For hop; a pruned map capped at 10k keys; input is never logged (SEC-2).
- READMEs updated: `src/editor/README.md`, `components/blocks/README.md` and `sections/README.md`.

**Known limit:** the 4-in-flight slot is held only while the action composes the page. Section data fetched while the tree streams is bounded by the per-IP limit, not the slot (documented in limits.ts).
built.tests:
`cd frontend/storefront && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` passes with no errors.

The storefront package has no test runner, so I wrote a scratch script (scratchpad `d4s/check.mts`, run with the backend's tsx). It passes and covers:
- `normalizeMotion` on null, string, array, `{}`, `'FADE'`, an unknown intensity and valid values.
- MOTION_SPECS covers every preset.
- `rangeCss` / `motionVars` output.
- `rangeProgress` / `rangeSpan` for the entry, cover and exit-crossing+vh ranges, against the §2.4 maths.
- `hasMotion`, top level and inside columns.
- `blockHref` neutralises `javascript:` (with mixed case and whitespace), a control-char prefix plus `data:`, and `vbscript:`; normal hrefs pass unchanged.
- The slug grammar, including kinds and invalid slugs.
- `sanitizeBlocks`: drops non-objects, bad ids and nested columns; caps columns at 4 and blocks at 80; drops a bad `conceptSlug`.
- `sanitizeSettings`, `sanitizePopupRules` (display falls back to modal), `popupContextSlug` and `sanitizeFonts`.
- `sanitizeFrameInput`: good input, a bad variant, a bad slug, a missing rev, bad blocks, TOO_LARGE measured in UTF-8 bytes with the rev kept, and a BigInt input.
- Limits:
  - 10 parallel acquires give exactly 4 slots.
  - 240 per IP per minute; the window resets after 60 s.
  - `clientIp` uses cf-connecting-ip only when cf-ray is present.

`protocol.ts` is byte-identical to `frontend/admin/src/lib/editorProtocol.ts` (checked with `cmp`).

As instructed, I did not run `next build`, `next dev` or any server. Headers, HTML regression and browser flows are left for the orchestrator's verification.

review.title: The render cap (SEC-2) covers only data loading, not the render, and a hung API can block every editor
review.scenario:
renderEditorFrame takes a slot, awaits loadFrameData (usually cache hits, about 0 ms), returns createElement(FrameDocument) and releases the slot in `finally`. The expensive part happens after release: React renders FrameDocument while it serialises the action response, including ManagedPage/SiteLayoutView/PageRenderer, every section's server render and the FeaturedMenu/Reviews/Kitchens/menu/location fetches. So nothing limits concurrent full-page renders server-wide. The only limit is 240 per minute per IP, and rotating IPs get around it. editor/README.md line 103 ('At most 4 renders in flight server-wide') and the SEC-2 'applied' note are therefore not true.

The opposite failure also exists. The fetches inside loadFrameData (fetchSiteLayout, fetchLiveConcepts, fetchBrandLocations) have no timeout. If the API accepts connections but stops answering, four requests whose cache entries have expired hold all four slots until undici gives up (minutes). During that time every operator's frame gets RATE_LIMITED, retries every 2 s and shows 'Too many updates at once; catching up.' instead of a clear failure.

Smaller point: `acquireRenderSlot` runs before `try`, and `sanitizeFrameInput(input)` is also called outside it. If the sanitiser ever throws, the slot is never released, and after 4 such throws the action is RATE_LIMITED until the process restarts.
review.fix: (1) Bound the composition fetches: pass AbortSignal.timeout(~5000) (or an equivalent race) to the fetches made by cachedLiveLayout, cachedConcepts and previewLocation, so a hung API can only hold a slot for a few seconds; on timeout return null/[] (pages fall back to their built-in design) or RENDER. (2) Move `sanitizeFrameInput` inside the try/finally. (3) Either keep the slot until the response has finished streaming (for example, release it on a short timer of about 3 s after return, or when the same IP's next call arrives), or correct the README and the SEC-2 note to say the cap covers composition only and renders are bounded by the per-IP limit alone.

review.title: edited:null accepts any slug, so anyone can force uncached API calls and flush the frame's live-layout cache
review.scenario: The only legitimate caller of `edited: null` is the pop-up backdrop, whose slug is either 'servd:home' or 'brand:<one targeted brand>' (popupContextSlug). sanitizeFrameInput accepts edited:null with any slug that matches the grammar. Example: {rev:1, slug:'page:<random>', edited:null, variant:'a'}. loadFrameData then calls cachedLiveLayout('page:<random>'), which is always a miss and causes a real GET to /site-layouts/<slug> on the API from inside the render slot. cachedLiveLayout also does `if (layouts.size > 200) layouts.clear()`, so about 200 random slugs empty the whole cache, including servd:header, servd:footer and the brand chrome. A small unauthenticated script therefore keeps every legitimate editor render on uncached API round-trips, and, combined with S-1, can keep the 4 global slots busy so that real operators get RATE_LIMITED.
review.fix: In sanitizeFrameInput, when `edited === null` accept only `servd:home` or `brand:<b>` with b matching CONCEPT_SLUG (the two possible popupContextSlug results); anything else is BAD_INPUT. In cachedLiveLayout, replace the all-or-nothing `clear()` with eviction of the oldest entry (the Map keeps insertion order), so a flood cannot evict the chrome layouts that every render uses.

review.title: The public action returns raw server exception text to any caller
review.scenario: In the catch block, `error: \`${RENDER_ERROR_TEXT.RENDER}${detail}\`` with detail = e.message.slice(0, 200) is sent back verbatim. Anyone can call the action, and it is a returned value, so Next's production error redaction does not apply. Example: a servd:location draft where a concept has no name makes previewLocation throw TypeError "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'localeCompare')". Future loaders can leak internal hostnames or ports (ECONNREFUSED 10.x:3001) the same way. The contract asks that failures log only code, slug and size.
review.fix: Return only RENDER_ERROR_TEXT.RENDER (optionally with a short generated reference id) to the client, and keep e.message in the server log next to the code, slug and bytes already logged there.

review.title: The dev host exception for [::1] never matches
review.scenario: devHost compares bareHost(host) with '[::1]', but bareHost does `host.split(':')[0]`, so a Host of '[::1]:3002' becomes '['. In development, opening the storefront at http://[::1]:3002/editor-frame always gets the 404 with `frame-ancestors 'none'`, which contradicts the builder's note that '127.0.0.1 or [::1]' is allowed outside production. Only development is affected.
review.fix: Parse IPv6 hosts before splitting, e.g. `const bare = host.startsWith('[') ? host.slice(0, host.indexOf(']') + 1).toLowerCase() : bareHost(host)`, or drop '[::1]' from the check and the note.

fix.summary:
I checked all four findings against the current code. All four were real, and all four are now fixed; none rejected.

S-1 (render cap and hung API):
(1) Slot now covers the stream. limits.ts gives each slot a hold() as well as release(). After a successful return the action calls hold(), and the slot stays counted until the same IP's next call arrives (the frame waits for each render before sending the next) or 3 s (HOLD_MS) after the return, whichever comes first. So one editor holds at most one slot, and the server-wide cap now counts renders that are still streaming. Because held slots now count, I raised MAX_IN_FLIGHT from 4 to 6. Failures and RATE_LIMITED replies still give the slot back straight away.
(2) Fetch timeouts. A new withTimeout(p, ms, fallback) limits each data fetch to 5 s (FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS): cachedLiveLayout falls back to null, cachedConcepts to [], and previewLocation (FrameDocument.tsx) to {}. A timeout is cached for only 5 s, like any other miss. A hung API therefore holds a slot for at most about 5 s, and the page shows its built-in design. previewLocation also no longer throws on a location with no name.
(3) sanitizeFrameInput now runs inside the try/finally, so if it throws, the slot is still returned.
The editor README Load paragraph and the action's header comment now describe this.

S-2: edited:null is now accepted only for servd:home or brand:<b> with b matching CONCEPT_SLUG (new helper isBackdropSlug). These are the only two answers popupContextSlug() can give; anything else gets BAD_INPUT. The live-layout cache no longer empties itself when full. It moves an entry to the end of the list whenever it is used and, when full (200 entries, MAX_CACHED_LAYOUTS), evicts only the least recently used one, so a flood of random slugs cannot push out the header/footer layouts every render uses.

S-3: The caller now gets only "Part of the page couldn't be drawn. (ref xxxxxxxx)", where the ref is 8 random hex characters. The server log line holds code, ref, slug, size and the exception message (capped at 200 characters).

S-4: bareHost in middleware.ts now handles bracketed IPv6 hosts: '[::1]:3002' becomes '[::1]', so the development exception for [::1] matches. Other callers behave the same as before, since a bracketed host never matched a servd or brand host either way.
fix.prodNotes: MAX_IN_FLIGHT is now 6 and each slot can stay held for up to 3 s after its action returns. With more than about 6 operators on different IPs editing at the same moment, some will briefly see "Too many updates at once; catching up." (the frame retries after 2 s). Operators behind one office IP free each other's held slots, so they do not compete for slots. When a render fails, the reference in the editor's error text matches the server log line "[editor-frame] render failed" with the same ref, which holds the real exception message.

For that whole time a page with saved blocks stays on 'Loading the page...', Layers and the inspector are empty, and the amber banner never appears. An untouched page stays on 'Loading the page's design...'. Meanwhile the centre already says 'offline' at 12 s. Contract §7.3 asks for an 8 s timeout that leads to the error state, and the builder's README claims the catalogue 'gives up after 8 s'.
review.fix: In useSectionCatalog add `retry: false`, or `retry: (n, e) => n < 1 && !(e instanceof SectionCatalogError && /within/.test(e.message))`, so a timeout is final. The banner already has a manual Retry.

review.title: When the first doc is too large, every repeated frame `ready` calls onReconnect and retries init
review.scenario: The working copy is over MAX_DOC_CHARS when the frame first says hello. sendDoc('init') refuses and returns false, so the frame never gets an init and keeps announcing `ready` every 1 s, up to 15 times. Each one passes the INIT_ECHO_MS guard because initAt is still 0 or old. The handler then runs again: it serialises and measures the large doc, tries init again, and since `wasLive` is true it calls `cb.current.onReconnect()`. That bumps previewReset about 15 times. The frame meanwhile stays on 'Loading the page…'.
review.fix: In the `ready` branch, when needInit is already true and the last attempt was refused as too large (tooLarge state or a ref), return early without calling onReconnect. Only call onReconnect when a previous init actually reached the frame (initAt.current > 0).

review.title: The preview slider stays enabled when the newest edit was too large to send
review.scenario: An edit pushes the doc over the size cap. LiveCanvas does not post it, so postedRev is unchanged, `updating` stays false, and only `error` is set. `motionPreview.ready` is `connection === 'live' && !frame.updating`, so the slider stays enabled. It then scrubs the element on a stale page that no longer matches the inspector, for example after the preset was just changed. Contract §7.5 says the slider is enabled only when the frame shows the latest edit.
review.fix: Expose the too-large state, or a 'latest edit not drawn' flag, in FrameStatus. Disable the slider in that case with the reason 'Updating the page…' or the too-large text, e.g. `ready: frame.connection === 'live' && !frame.updating && !frame.stale`.

fix.summary:
I checked all three findings against the code. All three were real and all three are fixed; I rejected none.

A-1 (catalogue timeout could take about 17 s): `SectionCatalogError` now records whether the storefront hung past the 8 s limit. `useSectionCatalog` sets `retry: (failures, err) => failures < 1 && !(err instanceof SectionCatalogError && err.timedOut)`, which overrides the app-wide `retry: 1`. A hang now reaches the error state at 8 s, and the banner's Retry button stays the manual way to try again. A fast failure (refused connection, HTTP error, bad JSON with no timeout) is still retried once. The README sentence about the 8 s limit now says this.

A-2 (repeated `ready` messages after a too-large first doc): `LiveCanvas` keeps a `tooLargeRef` next to the `tooLarge` state, set in `sendDoc`. While the frame is still waiting for an init that was refused as too large, its repeated `ready` messages return early. They no longer re-measure the doc, try the init again or call `onReconnect`; the init goes out through `flushDoc` once an edit brings the doc under the cap. `onReconnect` now fires only when an earlier init actually reached the frame (`initAt.current > 0`), replacing `wasLive || renderedRev > 0`.

A-3 (preview slider still on after a too-large edit): `FrameStatus` has a new `stale: boolean` field, true when the newest edit was too large to send. In `Builder`, the slider's `ready` is now `connection live && !updating && !stale`. When stale, the slider explains: "The page is too large to preview, so it doesn't show your latest change." When `stale` turns true, a preview that is running is ended: the builder posts progress null for the selected element and resets the preview counter, so the slider goes back to "live". `missingIds` also skips a stale page.
fix.tests: `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` in `frontend/admin` passes with no errors. The admin has no unit-test harness for these components, so there are no new automated tests. No backend files were touched in this pass, so vitest was not needed. The orchestrator's browser flows should check three things: with the storefront hanging, the amber banner appears at about 8 s; a doc over 600 KB shows the too-large chip and a disabled slider; the frame keeps showing the loading screen without repeated reconnect resets.
fix.amendmentsApplied: A-1 is fixed in a slightly different way from the reviewer's suggestion. There is a `timedOut` flag on `SectionCatalogError` instead of `retry: false` or matching the error text, so only a hang is final and quick failures still get one retry. A-3 goes one step further than suggested: when the page goes stale, any running preview is also ended in the frame.

review.title: motion: null on a column child is stored as null, not stripped as §1 requires
review.scenario: The admin PUTs a draft with a columns block whose child is { id:'x', type:'text', motion:null }. blockSchema validates the column children through columnsFields.safeParse(b) inside superRefine, which only forwards issues. The children's parsed output is thrown away, and the raw `columns` array goes through passthrough unchanged. I checked this with tsx: blocksSchema.parse([{type:'columns', columns:[[{id:'x',type:'text',motion:null}],[...]]}]) returns the child with "motion":null. Top-level blocks and settings.ab.blocks do drop the key. The contract says 'null is accepted and stripped (parsed value undefined → dropped from stored JSON)' and covers column children explicitly. The 'motion: null is dropped' test only checks a top-level block, so the summary's claim is broader than what the code does for columns. The renderers I checked (storefront normalizeMotion, mobile motionPreset) treat null as none, so this only affects stored-data hygiene and copy consistency. It breaks no page today, but any future consumer that does `'motion' in b` or `b.motion !== undefined` would read a column child as having motion.
review.fix: Make columns validation produce the parsed children. For example, in blockSchema use `blockBase.transform` / `superRefine` + `transform`, or parse with columnsFields and return `{ ...b, columns: parsed.columns }` when it succeeds. Alternatively, strip `motion: null` in a preprocess on leafBlockSchema's input before passthrough. Then add a schema test and a route test: a column child with `motion:null` ends up without the key after a JSON round trip.

fix.summary: M-1 was a real bug and it is fixed. The reviewer was right: `blockSchema` checked `columns` children with `columnsFields.safeParse` inside `superRefine` and then threw the parsed result away. The raw children went through passthrough, so a column child's `motion: null` was stored as `null` and not dropped. `blockSchema` is now `blockBase.transform(...)`. For a `columns` block it parses `columnsFields` and returns `{ ...b, columns: r.data.columns }`, so column children follow the same rules as top-level blocks. A failed parse still forwards its issues, so a bad block is still a 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`. Non-columns blocks still run `checkLeaf` and come back unchanged. As a result, `motion: null` is now dropped at the top level, in column children and inside `settings.ab.blocks` columns, which is what §1 asks for. The module README already said `null` is dropped, and that is now true everywhere. One side effect: column children now come out in zod's key order, as top-level blocks already did. Their content is the same, and Postgres jsonb does not keep key order anyway. Nothing else from the review was left unfixed or rejected.
